builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DStill: Trajectory Consistency Distillation for Accelerated One-Step Drafting in Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding
summary: The method replaces iterative multi-step refinement in block-diffusion speculative drafting with a distilled one-step student trained on the drafter's own refinement trajectories. It requires a two-stage training pipeline, curriculum from partially revealed to fully masked blocks, and access to a block-diffusion drafter compatible with the target model family. It can fail if the one-step student retains token factorization errors on out-of-distribution prompts or if acceptance length degrades on tasks underrepresented in the trajectory curriculum.
rationale: The result is promising but depends on training infrastructure and model-family-specific diffusion drafters that a constrained team is unlikely to reproduce without published artifacts.
technique: Trajectory consistency distillation for one-step block-diffusion drafting

claims.statement: The method replaces iterative multi-step refinement in block-diffusion speculative drafting with a distilled one-step student trained on the drafter's own refinement trajectories. It requires a two-stage training pipeline, curriculum from partially revealed to fully masked blocks, and access to a block-diffusion drafter compatible with the target model family. It can fail if the one-step student retains token factorization errors on out-of-distribution prompts or if acceptance length degrades on tasks underrepresented in the trajectory curriculum.
DStill improves acceptance length by up to 28% and speedup by up to 25% over one-step DFlash, achieving up to 6.45x speedup over auto-regressive decoding.
